run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T07:49:15Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: frontend-proxy is returning HTTP 504 to callers because its upstream frontend stops answering product-catalog-dependent requests: frontend-proxy's own Envoy access log records '504 UT response_timeout' with a 15000 ms response flag against upstream 'frontend 100.96.4.150:8080' on /api/products/*, /api/recommendations and /api/checkout, while /api/cart and /api/data on the same upstream still return 200 in a few milliseconds, and product-catalog completed zero spans in the final 10 minutes of the window. The fault on product-catalog is a recurring Chaos Mesh network-delay experiment: the chaos-mesh Schedule 'otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay' spawned a new NetworkChaos object every minute from 07:47:14Z, and each one logged 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9' with matching PodNetworkChaos updates on that pod, recovering about 55 s later before the next was spawned. 504s were already being logged at 07:47:56Z, before the alert's 07:49:15Z start. All otel-demo pods are Running/ready with zero restarts (except fraud-detection), the product-catalog and frontend Deployments are Available with 1/1 ready, and the product-catalog application log shows normal 'Product Found' activity with no errors, so this is a network-level injection on the product-catalog pod rather than an application crash or a manifest/service misconfiguration. The mechanism by which packets are delayed (delay value, direction, correlation) could not be read, and the alerting rule itself returned no data.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own span error signal is real and rising: its span status values are STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET, and the 5-minute error-span rate for span_name 'ingress' moved from 0 at the 07:53 evaluation point to 0.963 at 07:56, 2.426 at 07:59, 2.407 at 08:02 and 2.007 at 08:05, while the non-error (UNSET) ingress rate fell from about 12.8 to 2.07 at 07:59 and 0.57 at 08:02.

frontend-proxy (Envoy) access logs record '504 UT response_timeout' with duration 15000/15001 ms and upstream 'frontend 100.96.4.150:8080' for GET /api/products/*, GET /api/recommendations?productIds=* and POST /api/checkout, while in the same minutes POST /api/cart, GET /api/cart and GET /api/data against the same upstream return 200 'via_upstream' in 3-249 ms.

Proxy 504 timeouts were already being written at 07:47:56-07:47:59Z (5 matching lines shown for the 07:44:00-07:48:00 range, 104 matching lines in total in that range) and at 07:49:54-07:49:59Z (366 matching lines in 07:44:00-07:50:00), i.e. the error onset precedes the alert's 07:49:15Z start.

Trace f2dd787005542001fa63d417d7a7940d shows the failure path with visible parent references: load-generator 'GET' span status error=true http.status_code=504 (15,002,511 us) -> frontend-proxy 'ingress' span error=true http.status_code=504 (15,001,077 us) -> frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' span error="true" http.status_code="0" (15,000,678 us, parent of a frontend 'GET' span of 15,000,142 us that itself reports http.status_code=200).

The sampled frontend-proxy spans from 07:56:11-07:56:44Z are dominated by 15-second ingress spans carrying http.status_code 504 with otel.status_code=ERROR, plus one ingress/egress pair with http.status_code 500 at 8.55 s, alongside sub-second 200 spans.

With a comparable baseline from the same metric and label set: for service_name="frontend", span_name="GET", the 10-minute window ending 07:40:00Z had 5200.97 spans total with 4861.84 at or below 100 ms and none above 5000 ms, whereas the 10-minute window ending 08:04:00Z had 826.45 spans total with 272.49 at or below 100 ms, 638.06 at or below 15000 ms and therefore roughly 188 spans above 15000 ms.

product-catalog produced no completed spans in the 10 minutes ending 08:04:00Z (increase of 0 for le 100.0, 1000.0 and +Inf), and its UNSET span rate fell from 13.36 at 07:40 through 10.02 at 07:49 to 2.55 at 07:52, 0.33 at 07:55, 0.0037 at 07:58 and 0 at 08:01.

product-catalog's application log shows only normal lines ('Product Found', 'Reloading Product Catalog...', 'Loaded 10 products') with no error lines, the newest line read being 2026-11-17T07:54:28.521305Z; the pod has no previous container instance.

The chaos-mesh Schedule named 'otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay' (namespace chaos-mesh) spawned a new child object every minute at 07:47:14, 07:48:14, 07:49:14, 07:50:14, 07:51:14, 07:52:14, 07:53:14, 07:54:14 and 07:55:14Z (events 'Create new object: otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay-jj42n', -6rtdg, -bx27q, -x5l64, -b5dxg, -gjgf2, -d9vpw, -26dqc, -hcwrz), and PodNetworkChaos events for pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9 were updated at each minute boundary and at each recovery (-:09 seconds).

Each spawned NetworkChaos object declares its target: 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9' is logged on NetworkChaos otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay-jj42n at 07:47:14Z and on -6rtdg at 07:48:14Z, with 'Time up according to the duration' and 'Successfully recover chaos for otel-demo/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9' about 55 seconds later on each object.

Event counts across all namespaces for the retained event range (07:30:07-07:55:14Z) group the fault activity on chaos-mesh NetworkChaos (9 Applied, 8 Recovered, 8 TimeUp, 9 Started, 68 Updated) and otel-demo PodNetworkChaos (17 Updated); the only otel-demo Pod events are fraud-detection container Pulled/Created/Started at 07:43:30Z, and no Evicted or OOMKilling events appear in that grouping.

The frontend, frontend-proxy and product-catalog pods in otel-demo are all phase Running, ready=true with restartCount 0 (container images ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend, -frontend-proxy, -product-catalog), and the corresponding Deployments report spec.replicas 1 with readyReplicas 1, availableReplicas 1 and Available=True/Progressing=True.

The product-catalog, frontend and frontend-proxy Services exist with selector opentelemetry.io/name set to product-catalog, frontend and frontend-proxy respectively, all exposing port 8080 to targetPort 8080, so the names used by the 504 log lines ('frontend 100.96.4.150:8080') resolve to an existing Service definition.

frontend also carries its own error spans in this window: status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR rate for service_name="frontend" is 0 at every point through 07:52, then 0.404 at 07:55, 0.233 at 07:58 and 0.875 at 08:01, while its UNSET span rate fell from 55.5 at 07:46 to 17.4 at 07:52 and 2.85 at 08:01; recommendation fell from 2.78 at 07:46 to 0 at 07:55 and checkout from 9.57 to 0.45 at 08:01.

The recurring NetworkChaos objects spawned by chaos-mesh Schedule 'otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay' delay traffic to/from pod otel-demo/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9; frontend's product-catalog-backed routes then hang until frontend-proxy's 15 s upstream response timeout expires, producing the 504 'UT response_timeout' error spans that drive the RequestErrorRate alert. The individual NetworkChaos object names differ every minute (-jj42n, -6rtdg, ...), so the persistent object is the Schedule.

frontend and frontend-proxy are not application-failing: during the same minutes that /api/products returned 504, the same Envoy upstream served POST /api/cart, GET /api/cart and GET /api/data with 200 in 3-249 ms, and both pods are Running/ready with 0 restarts, so the timeout is specific to product-catalog-dependent routes rather than a frontend outage.

product-catalog itself was not crashing or logging errors while the delay was applied: its container was ready with 0 restarts, had no previous container instance, and its log contains only normal 'Product Found'/'Loaded 10 products' lines, which argues against an application-level fault, an OOMKill or a restart as the reason its spans stopped completing.

fraud-detection was considered as a candidate cause because its pod has restartCount 2 with lastState.terminated.reason OOMKilled, exit code 137, and its container was re-Started at 07:43:30Z during the window; it is rejected as the cause of this alert because its own error-span rate stayed at background level (0 to 0.0037 per second, versus frontend-proxy's 2.43 per second) and the frontend-proxy failures are 15 s UT response_timeout errors to upstream frontend on product-catalog-backed routes, not calls to fraud-detection.

As a human follow-up (not executed here): inspect and suspend/delete the chaos-mesh Schedule 'otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay' if the delay is no longer intended, and verify from its NetworkChaos spec which delay value, direction and correlation are being injected into pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9.

gaps: The alerting rule's own expression and value could not be verified: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and with type=alert both returned no data, so the reported 'current: 1.422222222222222' cannot be tied to a specific PromQL expression.

The NetworkChaos and Schedule custom resources could not be read: chaos-mesh CRD kinds are not in the permitted Kubernetes resource list, so the injected delay value, direction, correlation, target mode and duration remain unknown, and the Schedule's continued activity after the last retained event (07:55:14Z) is unverified.

Retained events cover only 07:30:07-07:55:14Z and Jaeger returned frontend-proxy spans only from 07:56:11Z onward (frontend-proxy trace source_start_at 07:56:11.201603Z), so the earliest seconds of the error onset and any spans before 07:56 are unknown; the exact first 504 timestamp is not established.

A baseline query at 2026-11-16T20:00:00Z for frontend-proxy span rates returned no data, so no previous-day baseline exists in this target; the comparison here is limited to 07:30-07:40Z versus 07:54-08:04Z from the same series.

A cluster-wide listing of kind networkpolicies returned 0 objects (status no_data), so policy-based blocking was not verifiable either way; a frontend pod log query filtered for error|timeout|deadline|504 also returned no data (no lines matched, not a clean bill of health).
Secrets such as the flagd feature-flag configuration cannot be read, so a flag-driven fault contribution (for example a delay flag consumed by an application) could not be checked.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no deployment or configuration change record could be correlated with the 07:47Z onset.
Whether callers beyond the load-generator were impacted, and downstream/customer impact, was not observed in this data.
next_steps: Read the chaos-mesh Schedule 'otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay' (namespace chaos-mesh) and its child NetworkChaos specs to record the configured delay, loss, direction and duration.

Confirm with the platform owner whether the product-catalog network-delay experiment is intentional; if not, suspend the Schedule and re-check frontend-proxy 504s on /api/products, /api/recommendations and /api/checkout.
Fetch the Alertmanager rule definition for RequestErrorRate to reconcile the reported value 1.4222 with the observed 2.43/s ingress error-span rate at 07:59Z.
